Check that a control analysis shows its bias

Source: R/recovery.R
expect_biased.Rd

expect_biased() checks that the estimate of a control analysis is biased over the simulations of a fake scenario. Use it for an analysis that MUST be wrong, for example a crude model in a scenario with a confounder.

Usage

expect_biased(x, truth, estimate = "estimate", by = NULL, label = NULL)

Arguments

x

The stacked results of one analysis kind, for example results$models. It is a data.frame with the column sim that save_results() adds. It has one row for each simulation, or for each simulation and group of by.

truth

The true value of the estimate. One number for every group, or a data.frame with the columns of by and a column truth, with one row for each group.

estimate

The name of the column of x that holds the estimate.

by

NULL, or the names of the columns of x that split it into groups, for example "term". Each group gets its own assertions.

label

NULL, or one string that starts the text of each assertion. NULL uses the expression of x, for example "results$models". Give a label when x is not a named object, or for two calls on one object.

Value

A data.frame with the columns assertion, expected, observed and pass, and one row for each group.

Details

A control analysis shows that the fake scenario can find the error it was built for. When a crude model is not biased, the confounder of the scenario is too weak, and the recovery of the adjusted model shows nothing.

For each group, n is the number of simulations with a finite estimate. The bias is mean(estimate) - truth, and its Monte Carlo SE is sd(estimate) / sqrt(n). The assertion passes when |bias| > z * MCSE, with the z of expect_recovers(), 3.89. Otherwise it fails, and the row says that the control did not show the bias it was built to show. The row shows the "can detect" value of expect_recovers(): the smallest bias that the assertion finds with a probability of 80%.

Below 100 simulations, the assertion fails with "too few simulations to check". It also fails when more than 5% of the simulations have a missing or infinite estimate, and when all estimates are equal.

See also

vignette("pbn"), which checks a crude model in a scenario with a confounder.

Other checks of fake scenarios: expect_recovers()

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- data.frame(sim = 1:300, estimate = rnorm(300, 0.9, 0.2))
pbn::expect_biased(x, truth = 0.5)
#>                                    assertion
#> 1 x: bias of estimate against 0.5, a control
#>                                                   expected
#> 1 |bias| > 0.0433 (3.89 MCSE); can detect |bias| of 0.0527
#>                        observed pass
#> 1 0.407; 300 of 300 simulations TRUE
